title: Change existing rows with UPDATE
description: Write a statement that gives every employee in the Support department (`department_id = 3`) a 500 raise.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: UPDATE ... SET ... WHERE
UPDATE table SET column = new_value WHERE condition changes only the rows matching the condition - leaving out WHERE would update every row in the table, which is rarely what you want.
Set salary to salary + 500 (the column can reference its own current value on the right-hand side), scoped with WHERE department_id = 3.
expected_behavior: Raises the salary of every Support-department employee by 500.
solution: UPDATE employees SET salary = salary + 500 WHERE department_id = 3;
explanation: SET salary = salary + 500 reads the current value and writes a new one in the same statement, per row - and WHERE is what keeps the change scoped to Support employees instead of everyone.

hidden_tests.check_query: SELECT first_name, salary FROM employees WHERE department_id = 3 ORDER BY id
